page: Amazon Web Services r7a.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with a 4-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, clocking at 3.7 GHz with dedicated physical core allocation and one thread per core. The instance provides 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. It features no bundled local storage, relying exclusively on network storage volumes, includes no hardware GPU acceleration, and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Synthetic and computational benchmarks demonstrate strong single-thread performance, highlighted by top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core tests (3077.67) and Geekbench single-core execution (2054.0). Text processing and single-threaded bzip3 decompression also place in the upper quartile. Multi-core compute benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core (6620.0), PassMark CPU score (10555.37), and clang software compilation, settle in the middle fifty percent. Redis SET operations reach 10.46 million operations per second, aligning with typical mid-tier throughput for memory-bound key-value storage.

Performance tradeoffs emerge in uncached memory streaming and large-scale model inference. While small-block cached read bandwidth reaches 592.0 GB/sec, uncached 256MB read bandwidth drops to 37.49 GB/sec, which falls into the bottom quartile alongside slow 7B LLM token generation. With dedicated physical cores and substantial DDR5 RAM density, the instance delivers predictable single-thread responsiveness and resource-dense memory capacity without hyperthreading contention. The hardware profile fits in-memory databases, Redis caching tiers, backend application services, and data extraction pipelines requiring 32 GB of working memory.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro System, featuring a 4-core AMD EPYC 9R14 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz with dedicated physical cores. It provides 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, delivering an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration contains no local storage and zero GPU accelerators, paired with a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark assessments, the r7a.xlarge registers strong single-core performance across stress-ng and Geekbench, alongside robust single-threaded decompression and text processing. However, multi-core metrics and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth operate at average to lower-tier levels. The absence of hyperthreading contention paired with generous DDR5 capacity offers efficient resource density for memory-bound tasks. The instance matches workloads such as Redis or Memcached in-memory caches, relational database instances, ETL data processing pipelines, and general memory-intensive microservices.
